title: Post-incident summary reminders + auto-generated summary stub (timeline + dashboards)
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Internal: incident-bot now auto-creates a customer-facing post-incident summary stub at incident resolution and schedules reminder nudges (T+1, T+3 business days) until the summary is published or explicitly deferred.
description:
Context: As part of Status Page Transparency Upgrades, we need consistent post-incident summaries that are derived from internal postmortems but safe for external sharing. This PR adds two things: (1) a reminder job that nudges the incident owner to publish a post-incident summary within the configured SLA window, and (2) an auto-generated summary stub that is created when an incident transitions to Resolved, pre-filled with a customer-facing template plus links to the incident timeline and relevant dashboards.

What this does: When an incident is marked Resolved in incident-bot, we create a new summary artifact (currently a Confluence page via existing integration) using the customer-facing template. The stub includes: impact summary placeholder, start/end times, affected status page components (if present on the incident), and a “Links” section with (a) the incident timeline in incident-bot, (b) the incident metrics dashboard filtered by incident_id, (c) the component dashboard filtered by status_component (if known), and (d) any linked internal postmortem doc URL (if already attached). We then schedule reminder messages to the incident owner in Slack at T+1 business day and T+3 business days (business-day aware) if the summary is still in Draft. Reminders stop if the summary is marked Published, or if the owner sets a deferral reason (e.g., ongoing mitigations) which records an explicit “defer until” date.

Why: Support escalations have repeatedly asked for post-incident summaries and timelines for partial outages. We need a workflow that makes it hard to forget and easy to produce consistent outputs without relying on manual copy/paste.

Scope/Non-goals: This does not publish to the public status page directly. It only creates/updates the summary artifact and sends internal reminders. We also do not attempt to auto-generate root cause text; we keep the “Root cause category” field as a controlled dropdown placeholder to be selected by the owner. Redaction guidance remains in the Confluence template and external comms policy; this bot helps with structure and links.

Implementation notes: Added SummaryStore + SummaryStatus model; summary creation is idempotent on incident_id. Reminders are implemented as a scheduled job using the existing worker framework. Business-day calculations use the oncall calendar timezone (default America/Los_Angeles; overridable per incident). Dashboard links use the new canonical URLs from observability-pack; if a component is missing we fall back to incident_id-only filters.

Config: New config keys (with defaults): post_incident_summary.enabled, post_incident_summary.template_id, post_incident_summary.reminders.t_plus_1_bd, post_incident_summary.reminders.t_plus_3_bd, post_incident_summary.defer_max_days.

Testing: Unit tests for idempotent stub creation, reminder scheduling, and business-day calculations (including weekends). Added an integration test with mocked Confluence + Slack clients to ensure we don’t spam reminders when summary is Published.

Rollout: Feature flagged behind POST_INCIDENT_SUMMARY_WORKFLOW=1. We’ll enable in one region/oncall rotation first (per ENG-4821 rollout plan).

feat(summary): create Confluence stub on incident resolved (idempotent)
feat(reminders): schedule T+1/T+3 business-day nudges until published
feat(reminders): add deferral flow with reason + defer-until date
chore(config): add post_incident_summary config keys + defaults
test(summary): add unit + integration tests for stub/reminder behavior
docs: update incident-bot operator README (feature flag + config)
illustrative_snippet: Pseudo-flow: onIncidentResolved(incident) { if (!flagEnabled) return; summary = SummaryStore.getOrCreate(incident.id); if (summary.status === 'Published') return; confluenceUrl = ensureConfluenceStub(summary, incident); SummaryStore.update(summary.id, { url: confluenceUrl }); scheduleReminderJobs(incident.id, ownerSlackId, nextBusinessDayPlus(1), nextBusinessDayPlus(3)); }

review_conversation: Miles Thornton: Can we make stub creation idempotent? We’ve seen state transitions fire twice when Slack command retries. Devon Price (author): Yup—added SummaryStore.getOrCreate keyed by incident_id and Confluence page lookup by a stable title suffix + incident_id; creation now no-ops if the page already exists. Tomáš Novák: Please ensure the reminder doesn’t trigger if the incident is reopened after resolved. Devon: Added guard: reminder jobs check current incident state; if not Resolved, they exit and reschedule is skipped. Aisha Bello: Dashboard links—can we include both incident_id and status_component filters? Devon: Done. If status_component is present, we add a second link to the component dashboard and keep incident_id dashboard as primary. Dr. Aisha Rahman: Redaction: avoid auto-populating anything that could accidentally disclose provider/account identifiers. The “Links” are internal, but the stub content itself may be copied externally. Devon: Agreed—stub now contains only timestamps, component names, and placeholders; removed automatic inclusion of raw error messages/regions-by-account. Also added a warning banner at top of template referencing the external comms approval policy. Miles Thornton: One more thing—business-day logic should be timezone aware. Devon: Implemented using configured timezone (default PT) and added tests for weekend rollovers. Approvals: Miles Thornton approved. Tomáš Novák approved. Aisha Bello approved. Dr. Aisha Rahman approved after latest push.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Miles Thornton. Feature remains behind POST_INCIDENT_SUMMARY_WORKFLOW=1 flag; rollout tracked in ENG-4826.
